paragraphs.source_en: My master has a pockmarked face; I hear that before the Restoration smallpox was quite the fashion. Seen from these present days, when the Anglo-Japanese Alliance has been concluded, such a face cannot help seeming somewhat behind the times. The decline of pockmarked faces is inversely proportional to the growth of population, and in the near future they will vanish altogether: this is a precise conclusion drawn from medical statistics, a brilliant judgment so sound that even I, a cat, have not the slightest room to doubt it. I cannot determine how many of the people now living on this earth have pockmarked faces, but judging from my own circle of acquaintance, among cats there is not a single one, and among humans there is only one; that one is my master. I feel exceedingly sorry for him.

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人是张麻脸，听说在维新前痘疮是很流行的。从缔结了“日英同盟”的今天看，这张麻脸未免多少有落后于时代之感。麻脸蛋的衰退与人口的增长成反比，在不远的将来麻脸会全部绝迹，这是从医学统计上得出的精密结论，是连我这个猫儿也毫无置疑余地的英明论断。虽然还无法确定现在生息在这个地球上的人，有多少是麻脸蛋，但从我所交际的范围来估算，在猫儿中是一只也没有的，而在人中，也只有一个人，这个人就是我家的主人。真叫我为他难过得很哩。

paragraphs.source_en: Whenever I see my master’s face, I cannot help thinking: ah! What sins in a former life could have made him carry such an odd, ugly face and shamelessly breathe the fresh air of the twentieth century? In ancient times, perhaps, it might still have carried a little authority. But now, when pockmarks have received orders to withdraw to the upper arm, for my master’s still to occupy the tip of his nose and both cheeks and stubbornly hold their positions is not only nothing to boast of, it must also concern the honor of pockmarks themselves. If possible, the best thing would naturally be to remove them at once. Surely the pockmarks themselves must feel uneasy remaining on a face. Or perhaps these pockmarks have ideas of their own: seeing their party’s power ever declining, they have resolved that they must, with the tenacity of dragging the setting sun back to the zenith, insolently occupy the whole face. If that is truly the case, one ought not to look down on these pockmarks with contempt. They are an everlasting aggregate of pits resisting the sweeping vulgar current of the world; one might call them unevenness most worthy of reverence. Only, they look rather dirty; that is their defect.

paragraphs.source_zh: 每当我看见主人的这张面孔，就不由得想：唉！真不知前世是怎样造的孽，才使他带着这张丑八怪的面孔，不知羞耻地呼吸着二十世纪的新鲜空气。如果是在古时候，也许还可以多少抖抖威风。但是，在这种麻子已接受命令，退居到胳膊上的今天，主人的麻子仍然盘踞在鼻头或两颊上，顽守着阵地，这不仅不足以自豪，而且也必然要关系到痘疮本身的荣誉。如果可能，本来马上就应把它们除掉，那是当然最好不过的了。其实痘疮本身在脸上肯定也觉得呆得不安稳啊。不过，这些麻子也许另有想法，鉴于同党势力越来越衰落，因而下定决心，不能不以挽落日于中天的顽强态度，蛮横地占据着整个面孔。如果真是这样的话，对这些麻子，还真不应该以轻蔑的态度小瞧它们呢。它是抵抗天下流俗的万古常存的坑点集合体，也可以说是大值得人崇敬的坎坷不平哩。只不过看起来有些肮里肮脏罢了，这是它的缺点。

paragraphs.source_en: When my master was a child, in Yamabushi-cho in Ushigome there was a famous Chinese-style physician named Asada Sobaku, and it is said that whenever this old gentleman visited a patient’s house, he always went swaying along in a palanquin. However, after old Sobaku passed away and the practice came to his adopted son, the palanquin quickly changed into a rickshaw. Thus, if that adopted son dies and the next adopted son carries on the family business, kakkonto may very well turn into antipyrine. Even in old Sobaku’s day, parading through Tokyo in a palanquin was already not a very presentable thing. The only beings who could do such a thing and remain unconcerned were old-fashioned dead men, pigs being shipped in railway cars, and this old Sobaku alone.

paragraphs.source_en: My master’s pockmarked face is no different from old Sobaku’s palanquin in its ill fortune; seen from the side, it is enough to discourage one on his behalf. Yet my master, as stubborn as that Chinese physician, still exposes his pockmarked face, like a lonely castle in the setting sun, to broad daylight and goes to school every day to teach his English Reader.

paragraphs.source_en: Thus he mounts the platform with the memorials of the previous century engraved all over his face. To his students, besides giving lessons, he must certainly be imparting a weighty admonition. He scarcely needs to repeat phrases like “the monkey has hands”; instead, with no effort at all, he explains the great question of “the influence of pockmarks upon the countenance,” and silently supplies the answer to his pupils. If teachers like my master were ever to disappear, these students, in order to study this problem, would have to run to libraries or museums and expend a labor equal to ours when we try to imagine the ancient Egyptians through mummies. Seen in this light, the pockmarks on my master’s face are, in some mysterious way, bestowing an unexpected merit.

paragraphs.source_en: Of course, my master did not plant smallpox all over his face in order to bestow this merit. Do not underestimate these pocks; in truth, they too were originally inoculated, only unfortunately what he had thought was planted in his arm somehow spread to his face. At the time my master was still a child and, unlike now, knew nothing of good looks, so he only kept crying, “It itches! It itches!” and desperately scratched at his face; it was like lava flowing over his face after a volcano had erupted, ruining beyond recognition the face his parents had given him. My master often tells his wife that before he had smallpox he was a boy as lovely as polished jade. He has even boasted, “When the family carried him to worship at the Asakusa Kannon temple, even Westerners kept turning back to look at that fair, plump baby.” Unfortunately, however, there is no one to bear witness for him.
